clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man with a history of cutaneous melanoma resected 2 years ago from the right scapular area, followed by recent re-excision of a skin lesion in the same location, presented to the emergency department with a right thoracic dermatomal rash (T2-T3 distribution) featuring dark red papular lesions with purulent discharge and grouped hard lumps palpated in the posterior axilla. The patient was confused on presentation. Initial clinical assessment raised consideration of herpes zoster given recent treatment history, and empiric acyclovir was initiated. However, skin biopsy of the lesions demonstrated cells strongly positive for S-100 and Melan-A immunostains with negative CK AE1/AE3 staining, confirming melanocytic origin and ruling out epithelial malignancy. This immunohistochemical profile, combined with the clinical presentation of dermatomal distribution rash, grouped axillary lumps, and prior melanoma history, establishes the diagnosis of metastatic amelanotic melanoma with regional lymph node involvement.
